title: Gunnar Wiegand on Protecting Europe without Starting a Trade War - The Wire China
gist: Two weeks after the latest Xi-Trump meeting, EU-China trade talks addressed a deficit widening by more than 1 billion euros a day; China agreed to limit hybrid EV exports, and the Q&A with Gunnar Wiegand asks how Europe can protect itself without a trade war. Only the teaser is available (paywalled).

insights.claim: The EU's trade deficit with China is widening by more than 1 billion euros a day, which Commission President Ursula von der Leyen warned had reached a 'tipping point'.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: A deficit this size raises odds of EU trade defence measures against Chinese goods.
insights.quote: an imbalance that European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen warned had reached a “tipping point.”

insights.claim: In trade talks with Beijing, China agreed to limit its surging exports of hybrid electric vehicles, which most observers hailed as an important step forward.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Watch European auto makers and Chinese hybrid exporters for the effect of the export limits.

insights.claim: An open question is whether the agreement is enough for Europe to protect itself without triggering a trade war.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Framing suggests EU policy remains torn between protection and escalation risk.
